elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms") and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied — the opt-out is 60 days (not ≤30) and no Vendor reminder obligation was added — so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence requires notice "at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term"; 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred maximum.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; the redline adds only a Customer non-renewal election and imposes nothing on Kubient.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal sentence renews on the same terms with no unilateral uplift, escalator or price-increase mechanic (fees are revenue share set in each Exhibit), so no cap is engaged.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Added operative sentence: "Customer may elect not to renew this Agreement by giving written notice of non-renewal to Kubient at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term, in which case this Agreement will expire at the end of that Term." The window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a scanning artefact — the operative text states "sixty (60) days" and the election is unconditional and Customer-exercisable.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: renewal is on the same terms with no price-increase or uplift mechanic in paragraph 4(a) or the renewal language. (The mapping's "already_met" quote is the auto-renew sentence, which contains no uplift right — correct in substance.)

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted sentence supplies a Customer non-renewal election on exactly 60 days' notice before the end of the then-current Term (≤60 days), and the price-cap element is not engaged because renewal carries the same terms with no uplift mechanic.

The deterministic "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" check reports "number not found", but inspection of the operative text shows "at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term"; the regex miss is mechanical, not substantive.

Preferred level fails on two elements: the opt-out is 60 days rather than ≤30, and there is no Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal. To reach preferred the drafter would need to change "sixty (60) days" to "thirty (30) days" and add an express Kubient reminder covenant.

Minimal: only one concise sentence is inserted; nothing is deleted, the retained mutual 90-day post-Initial-Term termination right and Kubient's fee entitlement survive, and no survival tail, expense, procedure or other extra requirement is added. The short "in which case this Agreement will expire at the end of that Term" tail is operationally necessary to make the election bite against the automatic-renewal sentence, not surplus.

Preserves intent: this is natural-term non-renewal (correctly handled under RENEWAL, not T4C), the 90-day mutual convenience right and paragraph 4(b) breach/insolvency mechanics are untouched, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling. The retained "unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions" is not contradicted because the new sentence expressly directs expiry at the end of the Term.

Note for the drafter (rationale-level, not a defect): 60 days sits at the fallback ceiling; if Kubient pushes back on drafting, do not let the window extend beyond 60 days, as 90+ days is walk-away territory.
